reviewNote: Drafted by Claude for faculty review from the Carson-Newman scenario. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Class III obesity with GERD and an adhesive SBO: dinner 10 hours ago, vomiting since 0200, distended stomach on CT, refused NG. The CN RSI rubric case: 3 minutes of 100% O2, cricoid, no mask ventilation before laryngoscopy, sustained EtCO2 before cricoid release.

asa.rationale: Class III obesity, HTN, prediabetes; urgent surgery.

decision.rationale: Urgent bowel obstruction; proceed with RSI and aspiration precautions.

redFlags.finding: Full stomach: SBO with vomiting and a distended stomach, no NG
redFlags.evidence: Vomiting since 0200 (last 0520); CT shows a fluid filled, distended stomach; NG refused.
redFlags.implication: High aspiration risk at induction regardless of fasting time.
redFlags.action: RSI with cricoid pressure, head up, suction ready, consider NG to decompress before induction, no mask ventilation before the first laryngoscopy.

redFlags.finding: Class III obesity (BMI 40.4) with reduced FRC
redFlags.implication: Fast desaturation during apnea; harder mask and laryngoscopy.
redFlags.action: Ramp position, 3 min preoxygenation at 100% (EtO2 90 or more), video laryngoscope available.

redFlags.evidence: Nightly reflux despite omeprazole; cannot lie flat.
redFlags.action: Aspiration prophylaxis (H2 blocker given, sodium citrate), head up induction.

redFlags.evidence: Loud snoring, daytime sleepiness, sleep study never done.
redFlags.action: Opioid sparing plan, monitored bed, extubate fully awake and reversed.

planItems.item: RSI: propofol or etomidate plus rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg or succinylcholine
Video laryngoscope and bougie ready; confirm with sustained EtCO2 before releasing cricoid
Cefoxitin 2 g within 60 min of incision
Extubate awake, full reversal (sugammadex), head up
